pillar_reactions.evidence: Engaged actively with the mechanism and asked to understand it rather than just accepting it. The rep opened with a pseudo-clinical framing - 'have you ever heard of something called cortical inhibition?' - which the prospect, a second-year medical student, had not: 'Maybe if you can write that in German, maybe. I only did like two years.' He then attempted the flexibility-versus-mobility distinction himself and pushed back on the rep's answer with a real question: 'Doesn't flexibility come with mobility?' He accepted the final explanation ('Yes, yes'). Worth noting he had already pre-sold himself on the modality before the pillar was delivered: 'I think that's why I think kettlebells are more healthy. These are just muscles that are just for the show.'

The primal eating protocol was never delivered on this call. Nutrition came up only as a discovery question ('How's your nutrition?') which produced useful material - he does not track calories, eats his mother's home cooking, and gained five kilos on exam-block sugar - and it was mentioned once in passing as something the programme would dial in. The pillar itself, the philosophy, the guidelines and the no-macro-tracking positioning were never presented, despite this being a prospect with a stated cut goal who had just regained weight.

Presented mainly as the thing that distinguishes the flagship from the lower tier - 'there's no personalization or accountability that you would get from working with Trevor directly... if you record yourself doing the movements, can make sure that you're doing it right' - and the prospect understood it precisely and traded it away on cost grounds: 'maybe I don't have someone who's always watching how my forum is, but I have a plan. You know, I have a community, I have a plan, and I know what I need to do.' He had earlier said accountability and guidance were exactly what he came for, so this is an accepted trade-off under financial pressure rather than a genuine low valuation.

anchors.raw: But right now I have, okay, let's say $900 left... So let's say 900, 200 of them are like an investment. I have 700 and maybe I'm ready right now. I hope you have these prices to spend right now on my health, 300, 400, let's say 300.
anchors.note: Proposed label: self_declared_budget_ceiling. The single most damaging anchor in the batch, and the rep created it by asking for it before quoting anything: 'like right now, like ballpark, like what do you have available to invest in your fitness'. Once $300 was in the room, $6,000 could only ever read as absurd, and the prospect's reaction confirmed it: 'Damn. Okay. Yeah. And far from it.' The number was also volatile and negotiable in his own telling - he moved from 900 to 700 to 400 to 300 inside one turn - which is exactly the state the financial-picture questions exist to work with rather than accept.

anchors.raw: But we also have our primal university, we call it, which is, it's, number one, it's month to month. Like, you can quit whenever... It's $199 a month.
anchors.competitor: Primal University - the company's own lower tier
anchors.note: Proposed label: internal_downsell_tier. Second appearance of this pattern in the batch, two days after the same rep did it on the Sean Stover call. Here it arrived immediately after the 6k figure rather than before it, so it functioned as a rescue rather than a pre-anchor, but the effect was the same: the flagship was abandoned within one exchange of the price being spoken, with no attempt to bridge.

anchors.raw: Because I always thought, okay, I spend time on YouTube or something, I will find a way, watch this, watch this. But then I tried it a long time. And now I recognize that, you know, the things I want to build my life, like medical school, then my own business, and etc. I don't have the time or then want to spend my time searching for things.
anchors.note: Proposed label: free_method_that_already_failed. The inverse of the anchor that sank the Sean Stover call, and a genuinely strong supportive one. This prospect tried the free route, judged it a failure, and articulated the value of paying in terms of time rather than money. It was never used - the rep did not price his time, did not contrast the cost of another two years of self-research against six months of guidance, and did not return to it when the budget objection landed.

anchors.raw: that's why I went to private university and they're already paying like 1,500 euros a month. So I think that's 1,700 dollars maybe or something like that, I know, every month. So for me, it would be rude, like from my perspective, to ask them any more things.
anchors.note: Proposed label: family_funding_he_refuses_to_draw_on. There is roughly $1,700 a month of household spend on his development already in the picture, and a strong personal rule against adding to it: 'that's something I want to do. I want to pay it myself.' This closes off the most obvious funding route and makes the absence of any instalment offer more consequential, not less.

unmet_demand.want: Supervised coaching with form correction, at a price a student can reach. He asked for exactly this in his own words: 'I want in sport, want somebody to guide me to health, to a perfect form.'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Supervision exists only inside the $6,000 flagship. The tier he could afford is explicitly defined by its absence - 'there's no personalization or accountability' - so the one thing he came for is the one thing his purchase does not include. No instalment path was offered to bridge the gap.

unmet_demand.want: Training that is safe and appropriate for someone currently carrying a shin and femur fracture, a post-operative shoulder with a suspected biceps tear, and nightly lower back pain at six to seven out of ten.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: There is no clinical screening step anywhere in the process, no rehabilitation pathway, and no requirement for clinician clearance. The injuries were disclosed in the first two minutes and never revisited; he was then routed to the unsupervised tier, where nobody will see how he moves.

unmet_demand.want: A middle option between $199 a month self-serve and $6,000 for six months - something with some personalisation but not full one-to-one.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: No such tier exists. This is the second prospect in this batch to hit the same wall within two days, the other having asked for it explicitly by describing what he wanted as 'in the middle of it all'.

unmet_demand.want: A defined route back to the flagship once his web design business starts generating revenue - he stated plainly that he would buy it then.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Nothing was set up. No follow-up date, no check-in, no note of the trigger event. He said 'as soon as I can afford it, I know I will do it' and the call ended with a YouTube link and no mechanism to return to him.
